findings.reason: an absolute 10 s ceiling can red a correct implementation when the fleet node is loaded, sending the node to re-derive a fix that already works; naming the measure as a ratio to a same-session clean run, or a larger ceiling, changes what the node proves.
findings.text: the arm "the first `git diff --name-only` outside the fence ... finishes in under 10 s" is an absolute bar set against a call the section's own evidence measures at 5.7 s clean (5.6 s of it "preload index", in `~/.cache/reckon-promotion-rollout/review29/main-thread.txt`), on a node whose recorded load ranged 50–85, so the arm has about 1.75× the clean floor and can fail for load rather than for the defect — the same evidence shows the right shape is a paired comparison (250.4 s then 5.7 s in one worktree)

response_events.note: §24's timing arm is now a ratio: the first call after a fenced index write takes at most twice a warm call made straight after it, against more than tenfold (250.4 s against 5.7 s) at base, so node load cannot fail it.
